# Taste profile

What Yuvraj likes, distilled from everything he has saved. Any AI helping him should
read this first and lean toward it: match the look, reach for the libraries and tools
he already saved, and build on his own ideas. The part above the generated block is
curated by Claude and updated whenever a new entry shifts the picture; the evidence
below is rebuilt from the notes on every filing.

_Last curated: 2026-11-12, from 73 entries (now including his own projects)._

## Who he is

- Video editor and builder at **Revolio Media**, a creative studio in Mumbai (see
  Revolio Media studio). Makes launch films, motion and effects, and also builds the
  studio's internal tools (ledger, SSD desk, Saturday-off tracker, website).
- Builds **Revolio Labs**, the experiments arm of Revolio: an AI creative studio app
  (live with a waitlist), a cozy 3D desk-diorama website, and many small games and
  toys. Wants an in-browser VFX feature like Ladybug.
- Ships his own desktop tools under **PXLVZN** (pxlvzn.in): a utility app hub
  (downloader, stem splitter, LUT matcher, file transfer, AI-tag remover), CanvasFlow,
  Vinyl for Windows (paid), and pxlengine, a Rust/Vulkan ray-traced 3D engine.
- Has shipped a lot: about 40 projects in [catalog/projects.md](catalog/projects.md).
  Most are browser games (PEAKD, SLANGDAQ, Punchline, Sixer, Bonk Court, Rohit Learns
  Ball, Munde Mode) and tools for editors. Build on these before starting fresh.
- Builds with AI agents a lot: Claude Code, MCP servers (he wrote Social Reader),
  agent-driven Blender and game tools. Prefers tools that ship an MCP server or a CLI
  agents can drive.

## Visual taste

- **Chunky, flat pixel art** with a tight two or three colour palette (orange, blue,
  periwinkle), pixel cursors and UI bits. See the Captcha launch film and the pixel
  mascots in the Ace Of Frames reel.
- **Textured, painterly illustration**: loose oil-pastel brushwork in warm sky blue,
  orange, ochre, olive and peach, set against calm off-white layouts with a bold
  grotesk wordmark and elegant serif copy (Second brand identity). Also code-made
  paintings with real brush strokes.
- **Bold product-launch motion**: big type, UI mockups animating, glowing cards,
  playful mascots, fast cuts. Launch films are a recurring save.
- **Clean stylised 3D**: low-poly or simple stylised models, readable top-down
  cameras, dark neutral floors with chunky coloured props, minimal HUDs
  (Lastmaglab shooter, Polyfork kits). Storybook proportions for characters (big
  head, small body, trailing scarf).
- **Stylised cartoon 3D, desi setting**: caricature Indian characters (big moustache,
  Gandhi cap, Nehru jacket) and everyday Indian street shopfronts in bottle green and
  marigold yellow with warm light (Sharma Sweets 3D style, the look for his Tukaram
  Munde game).
- **Painterly stylised 3D animation**: animated-feature look with chunky armoured
  characters, misty desaturated scenes, red ink outlines and bold red/blue accents
  (Impossible Weapon animation, made with Krea AI).
- **Polished dark utility UI**: a single compact dark card, glowing dot-matrix data
  viz, colour-coded categories, plain-language copy and playful particle feedback
  (Storage scanner UI).
- **Image effects as a look**: halftone, ASCII, dither, glitch, glow (Ladybug).
- **His own shipped looks** (from what he built): dark near-black UI with a single
  lime or yellow accent and hairline strokes (PXLVZN, PXL app hub, Revolio Labs,
  Punchline); cream-paper editorial with condensed ink serif (PEAKD); poster and
  stock-ticker typography (SLANGDAQ); film grain on dark teal and paper (Meter Down,
  NPCs on Strike); cozy golden-hour 3D dioramas (Revolio Labs site, Munde Mode).
- Not saved so far: photoreal, corporate stock, generic SaaS gradients.

## Games he likes

- Casual, free **browser games** with one clear hook, often **cricket**: daily
  Wordle-style guessing (Cricle), simulated chases (500-0), country face-offs.
- Daily challenge loops, shareable results, light humour.
- What he makes himself: **Indian, desi and Mumbai humour** (Munde Mode, Meter Down,
  SLANGDAQ, Sunny Sultan parody), cricket (Sixer, Rohit Learns Ball), party and
  social games (Punchline, Wedding co-op), and small music or stage toys (TV Stack,
  Runaway Light Rig).

## Stack and sources he reaches for

- **UI:** React with an open-source design system (Astryx). Wants agents to build
  better UI, so give them a real component library rather than ad-hoc CSS.
- **Web apps he ships:** Next.js + TypeScript on Vercel, Tailwind, Supabase or
  Postgres/Prisma; plain HTML and vanilla JS for quick sites and concepts.
- **Games:** three.js (most of his shipped games), Vite, Unity WebGL, Godot
  (shaders, 2D water, top-down 3D), Blender driven over MCP, Mixamo rigs.
- **Desktop apps:** Python (PyInstaller), SwiftUI and Electron, C#/WPF, Rust with
  Vulkan for pxlengine.
- **Assets:** Polyfork low-poly kits (MCP), Pixel sprite search, Patch, ARC's CC 3D
  files. Prefers free or Creative Commons assets with clear licences.
- **Mobile apps:** native Swift, no accounts, no cloud, when building solo.
- **Growth:** organic short-form video (TikTok slideshows), hook testing, paywall
  experiments.

## How to use this when helping him

- Designing anything visual: default to the looks above (pixel art, painterly
  pastel, bold launch-film motion, clean stylised 3D) and say which reference you
  drew from. Ask before going photoreal or corporate.
- Building UI or games: start from the saved libraries in
  [catalog/libraries.md](catalog/libraries.md) before suggesting new ones.
- Use his own words in each note's `why` and `## Raw` as the strongest signal.

Viggle Remake model  (topics/ai/2026-11-13-viggle-remake-open-model.md)
============================================================
kind: tool
type: video
topic: ai
added: 2026-11-13
source: https://www.instagram.com/reel/DfpPt63MPOT/
status: unread
why: Viggle AI's open weights to recast anybody in a video
tags: video-generation, video-editing, hugging-face, open-source, to-try

## Summary
![screenshot](./2026-11-13-viggle-remake-open-model.jpg)

Viggle Remake is Viggle AI's video-to-video "transformation agent", with open weights on Hugging Face (`Viggle/Viggle-Remake`). It recasts every character in a scene and keeps them consistent across cuts, can swap objects, change the background, restyle or add VFX, handles clips up to 2 minutes, and you keep chatting to fix a shot. The model card shows ~20B params, wan architecture, GGUF quants (4-bit ~14.3 GB, 6-bit ~17.6 GB, 8-bit ~22.3 GB) and a minimax-h3 community license. Hosted use is from $0.96 per 10 s at 720p.

The frame is a screenshot of Viggle AI's launch post on X with the "REMAKE" demo clip (a car driving down a country road) and the reel's creator talking in the corner.

## Raw
https://www.instagram.com/reel/DfpPt63MPOT/?psln=MXF4ZTUwdjdkeXAwYw==

Wiggle AI's open waits to recast anybody in a video.

## Notes
- Open weights: https://huggingface.co/Viggle/Viggle-Remake
- Reel by @asharasjad; caption: "RECAST ANYONE IN YOUR VIDEO. FREE MODEL."
- Useful for his video editing work (character swaps in footage).

tags: unity, rigging, animation, tutorial
style: bodycam first person view, gloved hands with pistol, striped test room

## Summary
![screenshot](./2026-11-13-unity-bodycam-ik-hands.jpg)

A @gamedevinspire reel showing bodycam-style first-person hands in Unity driven entirely by IK, "not even a single animation clip". Both arms use Unity's Animation Rigging package with IK targets; an Aim Target parented under the camera makes the gloved hands and pistol follow where you look, with the weapon lagging a few degrees for that shaky bodycam feel. The project files are offered via comment.

The frame shows the Unity Scene view: two gloved arms with orange bone joints, a move gizmo on the left hand's IK target, a pistol in the right hand, a black-and-white striped wall and a dark floor with glowing orange dots; the Animation Rigging panel shows "L Target".

RelayVSR video upscaler  (topics/ai/2026-11-13-relayvsr-video-upscaler.md)
============================================================
kind: tool
type: video
topic: ai
added: 2026-11-13
source: https://www.instagram.com/reel/DfpWJb0BauP/
status: unread
why: open weight video upscaler available in ComfyUI
tags: video-generation, video-editing, hugging-face, open-source, to-try

## Summary
![screenshot](./2026-11-13-relayvsr-video-upscaler.jpg)

RelayVSR is an open-weight (Apache 2.0) diffusion model for video super-resolution, published by Comfy-Org on Hugging Face as a single file and loaded natively in ComfyUI since Nov 5, 2026. The LightX2V team also retrained it as RelayVSR X2, a native 2x upscaler (45 FPS on an H100, flicker suppression, two checkpoints) aimed at MiniMax H3 clips, e.g. 768×1344 to 1536×2688. A comparison post says it upscaled a 5-second AI video to 4K in about 50 s on a 16 GB GPU (vs ~7 min with SeedVR2), with sharp hair and eyelashes but stronger skin mottling and slightly more vivid anime colours.

The frame is the reel's opening: a Hugging Models post on X showing the Comfy-Org/RelayVSR model page, with "OPEN MODEL ALERT!!!" and "FREE AI VIDEO UPSCALER. BLURRY TO 4K." overlays.

## Raw
https://www.instagram.com/reel/DfpWJb0BauP/?rpxt=MWFnc3dxNG11MmZmbQ==

Open weight video upscaler available at ConfUI.

## Notes
- Model: https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/RelayVSR
- Reel by @asharasjad (same creator as [[2026-11-13-viggle-remake-open-model]]).

source: https://www.instagram.com/reel/DfkvaoETdCl/

why: app idea for PXL, a data transfer system checker for when DIT is happening on a shoot
tags: pxlvzn, product-idea, desktop-app, video-editing
style: dark menu bar popover, blue primary button, plain status sentence

## Summary
![screenshot](./2026-11-13-dit-offload-checker-idea.jpg)

Idea for a PXLVZN app: a data-transfer checker for DIT (card offloads) on shoots, so nobody formats a card before every clip is safely on the drive. Sparked by **backed**, a Mac menu bar app that compares a camera card against the working drive, shows what's missing ("131 of 131 files aren't on T7 Shield yet. Don't format."), copies only the missing clips into the right shoot folder and verifies every clip.

The image is backed's promo: a dark menu bar popover for "Card A" with "Choose folder..." and a blue "New shoot..." button, the T7 Shield listed as the working drive, headline "Your card: 131 clips. On your drive: 0."

## Raw

App idea for PXL, it can be a data transfer system checker, like whenever I'm like DIT is happening on a shoot or something, this app can be used.

Cinematic film skill  (topics/ai/2026-11-13-cinematic-film-skill.md)
============================================================
kind: tool
type: tool
topic: ai
added: 2026-11-13
source: https://github.com/Moh4696/cinematic-skill
status: unread
why: agent skill for explainer content
tags: agents, claude, video-editing, open-source, to-try
style: cork evidence wall, archive photos with red string, stamps and highlighter swipes, rolling counters, one continuous camera move

## Summary
![screenshot](./2026-11-13-cinematic-film-skill.webp)

Cinematic Skill (MIT, by exploraX) is an agent skill for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and others that makes narrated explainer and documentary films entirely from code. Ask for e.g. "a 90 second documentary about the Wright brothers" and the agent researches and writes the script, records a voice, pulls public-domain photos from Wikimedia Commons with licences, and builds one continuous camera move over a single designed world drawn in Skia (Python), so stamps, highlighters and counters hit on the exact narrated word. It then adds synthesised SFX, an optional score and burned-in captions, stopping for approval after the beat table, the look and a 30 s draft. Looks: cork evidence wall, studio, blueprint, night.

The image is the final frame of the example film "Twelve Seconds": a cork wall with a US map (Ohio and North Carolina filled, a route from Dayton to Kill Devil Hills), portraits, a typeset letter, Langley's failed machine with stamps and the 1903 first-flight photo with counters.

## Raw
https://github.com/Moh4696/cinematic-skill

This is a skill, agent skill for explainer content.

## Notes
- Install: `npx skills add Moh4696/cinematic-skill` (or Claude Code `/plugin marketplace add Moh4696/cinematic-skill`). Needs skia-python, numpy, pillow and ffmpeg.
- Same author: Open 3D Skills (three.js scenes, scroll films).
- Related: [[2026-11-11-ai-tween-paint-harness]]

pxlengine 3D engine  (topics/tech/2026-11-12-pxlengine-3d-engine.md)
============================================================
kind: project
type: tool
topic: tech
added: 2026-11-12
status: read
why: so AI agents can make 3D and VFX shots by writing JSON, with no editor
tags: pxlvzn, own-project, agents, vfx, game-engine

## Summary
pxlengine (`pxl`): a headless 3D and VFX engine built for AI agents. An agent writes a shot as JSON, runs `pxl render`, looks at the PNG and revises; no editor. GPU path tracing, glTF models and HDRI skies, custom Slang shaders, millions of GPU agents and FLIP fluid, and CG-into-footage compositing with tracked cameras. Outputs PNG/EXR, MP4 or ProRes.

## Raw
For context, should we add like all the projects that I've already made with their particular tags from my GitHub, like GitHub and my Vercel account, like the Revolio Studio, Revolio Labs, the Pixel utility engine that I've made, the games I've made, Peaked, Tukaram Munde prototype that is ready, but we are currently building on it. We have a lot of games like pixel art games. Just for the context of the second brain and for the agents to pick from.

## Notes
- Possibly the "Pixel utility engine" he mentioned. Has a Blender integration and Python/TS packages.
- Fits his agent-native way of working: [[2026-11-09-blender-mcp-storybook-hero-workflow]].

TapMac trackpad app  (topics/design/2026-11-12-tapmac-trackpad-app.md)
============================================================
kind: website-ref
type: tool
topic: design
added: 2026-11-12
source: https://gettapmac.com/#price
status: unread
why: This is a cool app, and the website is also cool for building something similar
tags: desktop-app, website, inspiration, reference
style: black minimal landing page, bold headlines with italic emphasis, expressive mascot, tap-count diagram, testimonial wall

## Summary
TapMac ("tap your MacBook, start talking") is a macOS app that turns taps on the MacBook into actions: one tap for on-device voice dictation, two taps for AI text actions on selected text (explain, fix grammar, rephrase, summarise), three taps for clipboard history, plus smart modes like mute on calls and play/pause video. A menu-bar mascot called Tappy shows the app's state. It's private (on-device, no account), Apple silicon only, and sells for a one-time $7.99 launch price (later $20) with no subscription. Saved both as a cool app and as a landing page to copy when building something similar.

Website: black, minimal layout; bold headlines with italic emphasis; Tappy appears in many expressions; a tap-count diagram explains the one, two and three tap actions; a looping demo video, a wall of social-media testimonials, directory badges and a single-price section ("Get 100% back" for posting about it, 50% off code for India).

## Raw
https://gettapmac.com/#price

This is a cool app, and the website is also cool for building something similar

## Notes
- Read via a page fetch (no screenshot: the site couldn't be opened in a browser from here).
- Related: [[2026-11-12-disk-cleanup-app]] (another small Mac utility idea), [[2026-11-12-storage-scanner-ui]]

Storage scanner UI  (topics/design/2026-11-12-storage-scanner-ui.md)
============================================================
kind: style-ref
type: video
topic: design
added: 2026-11-12
source: https://x.com/kshvbgde/status/2120782192385355974
status: unread
why: If I ever make a disk utility app to remove cache and disk cleanup, this UI is really nice for it.
tags: ui, desktop-app, visual-design, inspiration
style: dark compact utility card, glowing dot-matrix storage bar, colour-coded categories, plain-language helper copy, particle dissolve on delete

## Summary
A short demo from keshav (@kshvbgde) of a Mac storage scanner: "storage scanner so good you'll want to fill your disk." One dark card shows used space (e.g. 357.8 GB of 512 GB) as a glowing dot-matrix bar split into colour-coded categories (Apps, Developer, Photos, Movies, Documents, Music, System data, Caches, Trash). Hovering a category explains it in plain words and offers one action ("Clear caches", "Empty Trash"); clearing makes that segment's dots scatter away like particles. Saved as the UI to copy for a disk-cleanup app.

![screenshot](./2026-11-12-storage-scanner-ui.jpg)

Frame: "289.1 GB of 512 GB used, Emptying the Trash ~/.Trash/Old exports". The bar's blue, green, pink, purple, teal, yellow and grey segments are made of tiny glowing dots, and the red Trash segment is bursting into particles at its right edge. Below, a three-column list of categories with icons and sizes, and a footer: "The Trash is holding 31.4 GB of things you've already deleted" with an "Empty Trash" button. Other frames show a "Calculating ~/Pictures/Photos Library/resources" scanning state and "Looking for things you can clear".

## Raw
https://x.com/kshvbgde/status/2120782192385355974?a=esFxqha7hweCnA-1X1s&s=46

If I ever make a disk utility app to remove cache and disk cleanup, this UI is really nice for it.

- Read via Social Reader (post text + 4 video frames, 18.6 s video).

## Summary
A reel from @thesoloentrepreneur.yt showing a "₹1 lakh website": a 3D web scene of an old Indian sweet shop, "Sharma Sweets, since 1965", with a stylised cartoon Lala ji (big moustache, white Gandhi cap, purple Nehru jacket, white kurta) standing in front of the shuttered shop. The caricatured shopkeeper stands centre-right, Mixamo-style posed. Warm, soft lighting.

## Summary

Orchestrator subagent prompt  (topics/ai/2026-11-12-model-routing-orchestrator-prompt.md)
============================================================
kind: technique
type: link
topic: ai
added: 2026-11-12
source: https://x.com/Ash_uxi/status/2120440737703825767
status: unread
why: I need to test this workflow on one of my next
tags: agents, claude, prompting, workflow, to-try

## Summary
An X post from Ashish (@Ash_uxi) on using Claude Fable 5.2 as an orchestrator: it splits a task into subtasks, sends hard reasoning and judgment calls to Opus subagents and fast, well-defined execution to Sonnet subagents, gives each one a complete blueprint, then reviews, merges and fixes their work into one result. He says the output was "insane". The value is the reusable prompt below.

Prompt:

> You're the orchestrator. Split this task into subtasks. Send deep reasoning and hard judgment calls to Opus, and fast, well-defined execution to Sonnet. Give each subagent a complete blueprint: the goal, full context, exact steps, constraints, the output format and what 'done' looks like. They should never have to guess. Then review their work, merge it and fix it into one final result.

## Raw
https://x.com/Ash_uxi/status/2120440737703825767?a=h1y8v9hoHmMoD0kJEc0&s=20

I need to test this workflow on one of my next

## Notes
- Read via Social Reader (text post, no media).
- To-do: [[2026-11-12-try-orchestrator-workflow]]

Munde Mode game  (topics/gamedev/2026-11-12-munde-mode-game.md)
============================================================
kind: project
type: game
topic: gamedev
added: 2026-11-12
source: https://munde-mode.vercel.app
status: read
why: the Tukaram Munde game idea made playable: a parody Mumbai food-safety raid sim
tags: revolio-labs, own-project, browser-game, indian-setting, threejs
style: warm toy diorama 3d, caricature indian characters

## Summary
Munde Mode: a parody top-down Mumbai FDA raid simulator, the playable form of his Tukaram Munde idea. Each day you get an inspection brief, start at a restaurant door as Munde, check fridges, thermometers and burners, log 3 to 5 violations, pick an action and face the Bombay High Court. Four restaurant tiers (street stall, budget udupi or biryani place, Irani family cafe, fine dining). Characters were made from GPT Image references via Hyper3D and rigged on Mixamo; rooms and props are procedural three.js.

Lens focal length guide  (topics/ai/2026-11-12-lens-focal-length-guide.md)
============================================================
kind: technique
type: video
topic: ai
added: 2026-11-12
source: https://www.instagram.com/reel/DfnLpaPoNIf/
status: unread
why: cinematography lens guide for prompting AI video (no comment given)
tags: video-generation, cinematography, prompting, reference
style: surreal pastel wide fields, masked characters, giant planet skies, bold orange focal length type

## Summary
A ~39-second AI-film reel from @lemon_carpet (made with Seedance) explaining how lens focal length changes a shot, so you can ask for it in AI video prompts. The point: "close-up" alone means nothing; the lens does. A 50mm medium shot is "what your eyes see", a 200mm close-up shot "from across the field" compresses the background so a giant planet looms behind the subject, and wide shots shrink the subject into a huge landscape. Useful as a cheat sheet for prompting camera language in AI video tools.

![screenshot](./2026-11-12-lens-focal-length-guide.jpg)

Frames: a faceless white-masked figure in chainmail and a sequinned cloak on a blue wingback chair in a green field ("Because close-up means nothing"); a person in a teddy-bear head and mint suit labelled "Medium, what your eyes see, 50mm"; the same bear at "Close-up, from across the field, 200mm" with a huge blue planet and pink clouds behind; a wide shot of the chair tiny in an empty field beside a lone petrol station under the planet. Surreal pastel look, bold white and orange labels.

## Raw
https://www.instagram.com/reel/DfnLpaPoNIf/?exln=NGpjOXc5NGVnaTB4

## Notes
- Caption: "Comment LENS and I'll send you my lens cheat sheet. #aivideo #seedance #aifilm #promptengineering #cinematography"
- Read via Social Reader (caption + 4 video frames). No comment from Yuvraj, so filed as a technique.
- Related: [[2026-11-12-impossible-weapon-knight-animation]]

Impossible Weapon animation  (topics/design/2026-11-12-impossible-weapon-knight-animation.md)
============================================================
kind: style-ref
type: video
topic: design
added: 2026-11-12
source: https://www.instagram.com/reel/Dfm8H07Pohc/
status: unread
why: Brilliant art style for animations
tags: animation, video-generation, 3d-art, inspiration
style: painterly stylised 3d, chunky armoured knights, misty desaturated battlefield, red ink outline accents, bold red and blue colour pops

## Summary
"The Impossible Weapon", a ~34-second animated short by INK (@ink.industries_) and Pascal Gautier, made with Krea AI. Two stylised armoured knights face off on a misty, grassy battlefield: a hulking dark knight with a blue plume and a nimble silver knight with a red cape who leaps in with a sword. Saved for its art style for animation: painterly stylised 3D that feels like a hand-made animated feature.

![screenshot](./2026-11-12-impossible-weapon-knight-animation.jpg)

Frames: (1) the dark knight in a fur mantle and blue cape, a huge blue plume on his helmet, standing over a sword in front of rows of faded soldiers and blue banners in fog; (2) a close-up of a giant blade slamming into mud, dirt flying, with thin red ink outlines on the metal; (3) the red-caped silver knight leaping mid-air with sword raised at the still dark knight, a teal streak across the sky; (4) a low-angle shot of the silver knight with a red plume and cross belt buckle raising a fist. Muted grey-green palette, soft fog, foreground grass, punchy red and blue accents.

TikTok slideshow playbook  (topics/business/2026-11-11-tiktok-slideshow-app-marketing.md)
============================================================
kind: advice
type: bookmark
topic: business
added: 2026-11-11
source: https://x.com/g_buildz_apps/status/2115637587817955761
status: unread
why: grow an app from zero with organic TikTok slideshows
tags: mobile-app, marketing, growth, reference

## Summary
A thread by greg_buildz on growing a new app from zero downloads with no ad spend, using organic TikTok slideshows. The steps: find your audience by saving viral slideshows in your niche, warm up the account for a day or two, post consistently even when the first posts flop, put real thought into the first-slide hook, and end with a soft CTA (the app logo, never "download" or the app name). When a post wins, study it and make five new variations. He says this got his own app to 14,000+ downloads.

## Raw
https://x.com/g_buildz_apps/status/2115637587817955761?a=tqT39_8LMb21Qv9XoTY&s=46

## Notes
Read via Social Reader (8-post thread, text only). Steps in his words:
1. Figuring out your audience: search niche keywords on TikTok, save every viral slideshow, interact with them.
2. Warming up the account: 1-2 days max, save and interact a bit, don't bot-like or TikTok restricts you.
3. First slideshow post: may take a week or two to get views; stay consistent, add slideshows to your story.
4. Hook is everything: first slide decides virality; emotional and relatable, with a matching sound.
5. Post consistently + good CTA: app logo at the end, never say "download" or the app name.
6. Double down on winners: study the hook, topic and engagement of the winner, make 5 variations.
7. Takeaways: grew his own app to 14,000+ downloads this way; offers it as a service.

Related: [[2026-11-11-app-growth-checklist]]

Procedural arm rig  (topics/gamedev/2026-11-11-procedural-arm-rig-demo.md)
============================================================
kind: library
type: bookmark
topic: gamedev
added: 2026-11-11
source: https://x.com/apekshik/status/2120224530367119758
status: unread
why: open-source rigged arm to reuse in my games
tags: rigging, animation, open-source, to-try

## Summary
@apekshik used an AI model to build one highly detailed, open-source rigged arm instead of "one-shotting" a whole game: realistic bone armature, weight-painted mesh, volume-preserving joints and muscles that swell as the fist tightens. The arm uses two-bone IK (you set the hand target, it solves shoulder and elbow) while the 38-bone fingers use FK, curling joint by joint and stopping on contact, so it can reach, grab and place a ball on a table. Live demo at procedural-arm-rig.vercel.app, code at github.com/apekshik/procedural-arm-rig, free to reuse in your own games.

![screenshot](./2026-11-11-procedural-arm-rig-demo.jpg)

Video frame: a skin-shaded arm on a dark post reaching for a blue ball above a wooden table ("Reach & grab, two-bone IK, contact-aware fingers"), with a skeleton view below. Other frames show pick & place, a clenched fist, a finger wave, and a rainbow weight-paint view.

https://x.com/apekshik/status/2120224530367119758?a=ChwWhzRfVZVOzMcLw7g&s=20

why: safest way to build mobile apps solo with Claude

## Summary
A tip from Jake Silverstein (@lazyjakee) for solo founders building mobile apps with Claude: have it build in native Swift, with no user accounts and no cloud storage. Keeping all data on the device is the safest setup when you're one person, since there's no auth or backend to secure or maintain.

Claude Code agent tree  (topics/ai/2026-11-11-claude-code-agent-tree.md)
============================================================
kind: technique
type: bookmark
topic: ai
added: 2026-11-11
source: https://x.com/voxyz_ai/status/2120199820887593304
status: unread
why: cost-efficient Claude Code agent setup to copy
tags: claude, agents, workflow, reference

## Summary
A Claude Code tip from @Voxyz_ai: a cost-efficient agent tree where Fable 5.2 (medium effort) is the root orchestrator and only delegates on demand, Haiku 5.5 handles finding files and running tests, and Opus 5.5 (medium) edits code. Fable then integrates and verifies the results, and switches to high effort only if it gets stuck. It follows Anthropic's new model selection guide, and the image is meant to be handed to Claude Code to set it up.

![screenshot](./2026-11-11-claude-code-agent-tree.png)

Image: an ASCII diagram titled "Cost-efficient Claude Code agent tree". Fable 5.2 medium is the root/orchestrator and branches to explorer (Haiku 5.5, finds files), worker (Opus 5.5 medium, edits code) and tester (Haiku 5.5, runs tests). They merge back into Fable 5.2 medium for integrate + verify, with a dashed branch to Fable 5.2 high "only if it's stuck". Footer: "Split useful work. Don't spawn every role."

## Raw
https://x.com/voxyz_ai/status/2120199820887593304?a=b908V0171pUheO52HyM&s=46

App growth checklist  (topics/business/2026-11-11-app-growth-checklist.md)
============================================================
kind: advice
type: bookmark
topic: business
added: 2026-11-11
source: https://x.com/freddyfvng/status/2120257766543512041
status: unread
why: what to try before giving up on an app
tags: mobile-app, marketing, growth, reference

## Summary
Freddy Fang's checklist, drawn from app experiments across 78k apps, of what to try before giving up on an app. On the product side: rewrite onboarding, test paywall prices, plans and trials, add a short calculation screen before the paywall, win back users who bounce, and focus on one funnel metric at a time. On distribution: post 100+ short-form videos, test hooks, run several creator accounts, use UGC creators and spark ads, run Apple Search Ads on competitor names, and build one feature people screenshot on their own.

## Raw
https://x.com/freddyfvng/status/2120257766543512041?a=aMcZIQLKES-6mNmKCC4&s=46

## Notes
Full post (read via Social Reader, text only):

Product & Paywall:
- Rewritten your onboarding at least 5 times and checked where users drop off?
- Tested your paywall with different price points, weekly vs annual, and trial vs no-trial?
- Added a 3-second calculation/loading screen before showing the paywall?
- Shown a different offer to people who bounced the next time they open the app?
- Watched a stranger use your app in person?
- Added a viral loop in your product?
- Focused on the improvement of ONE metric at a time (install -> trial, trial -> paid)
- Had Claude dig through your competitor's one star reviews and improved them

Distribution:
- Posted 100+ short-form videos across TikTok, Reels, FB, & YT Shorts?
- Tested 20+ different hooks and cut everything that did not hold past 3 seconds?
- Ran multiple creator accounts instead of relying on one page?
- Reposted your top 5% winning videos with new hooks?
- Paid different UGC creators and turned the winning clips into paid ads?
- Ran paid spark ads on ALL organic videos
- Ran Apple Search Ads on competitor names and intent keywords?
- Built ONE feature so good that people screenshot it without you asking?

Related: [[2026-11-11-native-swift-app-tip]]

Ship MCP server tip  (topics/ai/2026-11-10-ship-mcp-server-tip.md)
============================================================
kind: advice
type: bookmark
topic: ai
added: 2026-11-10
source: https://x.com/joncphillips/status/2119849328776819015
status: unread
why: ship an MCP server and a documented API with whatever you build
tags: mcp, api, documentation, agents, reference

## Summary
Jon C. Phillips (@joncphillips): "Whatever you're building, ship an MCP server with it, and document the API." Best replies: write the OpenAPI spec first and generate the MCP tools from it so docs and server can't drift apart, put each endpoint's description in the spec since that text becomes the tool description agents read, and return errors that explain what went wrong.

![screenshot](./2026-11-10-ship-mcp-server-tip.png)

Screenshot of the X post (09/11/26, 5.5K views) with replies from @Madeactual (OpenAPI-first tip, which Jon endorsed: "That's the way to do it!") and @itsarunc (clear error messages).

Roboflow re-ID tool  (topics/ai/2026-11-10-roboflow-reid-tool.md)
============================================================
kind: library
type: tool
topic: ai
added: 2026-11-10
source: https://github.com/roboflow/re-ID
status: unread
why: track one player across clips for sports video edits
tags: computer-vision, object-tracking, python, open-source, to-try

## Summary
`reid` is an open-source (Apache 2.0) Python package from Roboflow that turns a crop of a person into an appearance embedding, so the same person can be matched across frames, clips or cameras. It loads pretrained OSNet and FastReID models, works with `supervision` detections from any detector (e.g. RF-DETR), and includes benchmarks for re-identification. Install with `pip install -U reid`; docs at reid.roboflow.com.

![screenshot](./2026-11-10-roboflow-reid-tool.png)

Screenshot of Alex Bodner's X post announcing reid, with a demo video: football players boxed on a pitch next to a t-SNE plot where each colour is one player's track, showing crops of the same player clustering together.

## Raw
https://x.com/AlexBodner_/status/2119869708832805344?a=HlVPKugADUb2xcnfk1k&s=20
(plus screenshot of the post)

## Notes
Could be handy for sports video edits: tracking one player across clips.

Polyfork 3D assets  (topics/gamedev/2026-11-10-polyfork-3d-assets.md)
============================================================
kind: library
type: tool
topic: gamedev
added: 2026-11-10
source: https://polyfork.dev
status: unread
why: open-source three.js asset library agents can use over MCP
tags: game-assets, low-poly, threejs, mcp, to-try
style: low-poly, shared kit palettes

## Summary
Polyfork is a library of 3,000+ free low-poly 3D assets for three.js, Unity, Unreal, Godot and Blender, where each asset is a small program with knobs (colours, proportions, part counts) that rebuilds when you tweak it. Has themed kits with shared palettes, procedural terrain, configurable Mixamo-compatible characters, and exports GLB/FBX/USDZ/OBJ. Comes with a no-install MCP server at polyfork.dev/mcp (search_assets, get_kit, get_terrain, preview_scene...) so coding agents can pull assets directly.

## Raw
Add polyfork.dev. It's an open source three js library that can be used. It also has an MCP server, so agents can use it.

## Notes
- Licence: free for commercial use in games, no attribution; free mesh files are CC BY 4.0. Can't resell the .mjs source or HD editions. Paid plans: Pro $15/mo, Lifetime $200.
- Catalog repo: https://github.com/lucas-martinic/polyfork-catalog
- Related: [[2026-11-10-patch-gamedev-platform]], [[2026-11-10-arc-3d-art-dataset]]

## Summary
Ladybug is a browser-based effects studio for images, video, type and sound: 60+ effects and 300+ looks (halftone, ASCII, dither, glass, glitch, glow, depth), keyframe animation, sound reactivity, and object, face and hand tracking. Claude code paintings  (topics/ai/2026-11-10-claude-code-paintings.md)
============================================================
kind: technique
type: bookmark
topic: ai
added: 2026-11-10
source: https://x.com/jkeatn/status/2119874007382299087
status: unread
why: idea for game art: code-placed brush strokes instead of image models
tags: claude, generative-art, creative-coding, inspiration
style: painterly brushwork, invented artist styles

## Summary
Jake Eaton (@jkeatn) has been painting with Fable 5.2 in code. To answer the critique that AI paintings only emulate real art, he has Claude invent artist personas with a backstory and a consistent, period-identifiable style, then steers it while it revises the brush and paint engines. Each painting is a Python program of 1-2k lines that places every stroke (usually a few thousand) through a simulated paint engine with different bristles: no image model, no pre-rendering or tracing.

![screenshot](./2026-11-10-claude-code-paintings-1.png)
![screenshot](./2026-11-10-claude-code-paintings-2.png)

Screenshots of the X post text, plus two example paintings: a glossy yellow spiral tube slide on a blue-and-red tiled playground with clouds and a green climbing frame, and a huge red dragon's head looming over a crowded ice rink full of skaters. The post quotes @claudeai's launch post.

## Raw
https://x.com/jkeatn/status/2119874007382299087?a=qmaQJLw2n-8etCxrBCc&s=46
(plus 2 screenshots of the post)

## Notes
Idea worth trying for game art: procedural, code-placed brush strokes instead of image models.

## Summary
Astryx is Meta's open-source (MIT, beta) design system, used inside Meta for eight years across 13,000+ apps. ============================================================
kind: style-ref

style: textured pastel brushwork, warm painterly palette, serif plus grotesk type, airy off-white layouts

## Summary
Ayush Soni's (@ayushsoni_io) brand identity for "Second", an app that keeps the context of your work ("Never explain yourself twice"). The look pairs loose, textured oil-pastel paintings of people in open fields (sky blue, orange, ochre, olive and peach) with calm white cards, a bold grotesk "Second" wordmark, elegant serif copy and faint handwritten calendar notes on an off-white background. Saved as a visual design reference.

![screenshot](./2026-11-09-ayush-soni-visual-design-post.jpg)

Image: a painterly field scene, a man leaping on a green hill under a pale blue sky, with orange, pink and ochre crayon strokes below. A white card in the middle reads "Second / Never explain yourself twice. Second keeps the context of your work, so every project, tool and conversation starts where you left off." Other images: a woman in a blue top and white skirt twirling against an orange and blue pastel block ("Your colorful presence"), a web hero "Everything Second writes belongs to you." with stacked painted field cards, and a pastel landscape with handwritten Mon-Fri schedule times beside it.

## Summary

## Summary
A free daily challenge game in the style of Wordle: guess the day's international cricketer in 10 tries. Blender storybook hero  (topics/gamedev/2026-11-09-blender-mcp-storybook-hero-workflow.md)
============================================================
kind: technique
type: bookmark
topic: gamedev
added: 2026-11-09
source: https://x.com/rewind02/status/2119821740058546282
status: unread
why: repeatable Blender MCP character workflow for my games
tags: blender, mcp, 3d-character, animation, rigging, workflow
style: stylised storybook 3d, big-head proportions

## Summary
@rewind02 built and animated a stylised storybook hero (curly-haired boy, green tunic, brown boots, long orange scarf) in Blender by driving it with Claude Opus 5.5 through the Blender MCP. The key trick: give the scarf its own bone chain so it trails and swings behind every step. Saved as a repeatable 8-step character workflow for Yuvraj's games.

![screenshot](./2026-11-09-blender-mcp-storybook-hero-workflow.png)

### The workflow (from the post)
1. Connect Claude to Blender via MCP; send front, side and back concept images.
2. Prompt: "build this hero part by part: curly hair, green tunic, belt, baggy trousers, boots, long scarf".
3. Blockout: big head, small body, storybook proportions.
4. Layer the outfit in order: tunic > belt > trousers > boots > scarf.
5. Rig it, with a bone chain in the scarf so it can swing.
6. Animate one clip at a time: idle with a blink > turn > walk.
7. Add follow-through so the scarf lags behind every turn and step.
8. Review scene: grey floor, fixed camera, back-view concept in the corner; fix one thing per prompt.

"A scarf that trails behind makes a simple walk feel alive."

## Raw
https://x.com/rewind02/status/2119821740058546282?a=4tYjy-hUHaGuRBuPsQw&s=20

(with a screenshot of the post, saved above)

500-0 game  (topics/gamedev/2026-11-09-thechase500-cricket-chase-game.md)
============================================================
kind: game-ref
type: bookmark
topic: gamedev
added: 2026-11-09
source: https://500-0.com
status: unread
why: fun cricket browser games
tags: browser-game, cricket, game-inspiration, to-try

## Summary
A free browser cricket game: spin a wheel to land on a real World Cup squad (e.g. West Indies 1979, India 2011), draft players into the batting order where they actually batted, then watch a ball-by-ball simulated chase of 500 in 50 overs with live commentary and a final scorecard. Odds depend on your top-7 batting, your 7 biggest hitters and your 4 best bowlers; no keeper or captain costs a small penalty. Unofficial fan project.

## Raw
https://500-0.com

fun cricket browser games
